_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE STORE'S REFUSAL OF AN UNMODELED KEY IS NOT VACUOUS —
run it from the repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- sweep \
crates/mnemosyne-atomic/sweeps/unmodeled-key.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. An adopter measured that an inventory entry carrying an
undeclared `modality` loaded, was invisible to every read, and was erased by
an unrelated `set-inventory-status` that exited 0. Every map-shaped type under
the store now denies unknown fields, a source law holds that for types added
later, and the refusal carries the JSON path of the value it refused.
SO THE INJECTIONS ARE THE THREE SERDE SHAPES A KEY IS ROUTED THROUGH, AND THE
PATH. A plain struct (`InventoryEntry`, the adopter's case), a struct whose
skeleton is flattened (`AtomicSection` — serde refuses out of what the
flattened fields left unclaimed, a different code path), and a struct variant
of an internally tagged enum (`TypedObject` — the tag is consumed before the
variant sees the rest, and a comment in this crate once said serde could not
refuse there at all). The fourth keeps every refusal and drops WHERE, which is
the version of this repair an adopter holding a thirty-megabyte store cannot
act on.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file, so a run sent to a build machine leaves its evidence on a
throwaway copy.

injections.name: the-inventory-entry-reads-past-a-key
injections.why: the adopter's own case: the entry loads with the key, every read answers without it, and the next unrelated write drops it at exit 0. The law must name the type, the load must stop refusing, and the wire must stop refusing and start erasing

injections.name: the-flattened-section-reads-past-a-key
injections.why: a struct with a flatten is refused by a different serde path — the keys the flattened skeleton did not claim are collected and checked after it — so a refusal proven on a plain struct says nothing about a section

injections.name: the-tagged-object-reads-past-a-key
injections.why: an internally tagged enum hands its variant a buffered copy with the tag removed, which is the third route and the one this crate's own documentation said serde could not refuse on

injections.name: the-refusal-does-not-say-where
injections.why: every refusal still fires and none of them names the entry, which in a store of tens of megabytes is a refusal nobody can act on — the repair that looks finished and is not
